authors: Sidney W. Hess; Stuart A. Samuels
title: Experiences with a Sales Districting Model: Criteria and Implementation
establishes: First published sales-districting model: equalise workload/potential over contiguous units, solved by a location-allocation heuristic.
relevance: The benchmark any territory-division paper is compared to. Establishes that balance-based districting is 50 years old, so novelty must lie elsewhere.

title: Callplan: An Interactive Salesman's Call Planning System
establishes: CALLPLAN: interactive optimisation of salesperson call frequency by account, with an estimated response function.
relevance: Origin of the concave-effort-response tradition; the companion argument to Skiera & Albers on why linear utility is contested.

title: Sales Territory Alignment: A Review and Model
establishes: Formalises territory alignment as an assignment problem over sub-units with a survey of criteria and a solvable model.
relevance: Canonical statement of the problem this work generalises. Cite when framing scope.

title: COSTA: Contribution Optimizing Sales Territory Alignment
establishes: Maximises total contribution using an estimated concave sales-response function per territory, rather than balancing surrogates.
relevance: The strongest challenge to a linear utility. A referee will ask why the response function is not estimated; this is the paper they have in mind.

title: Fast Approximation Methods for Sales Force Deployment
establishes: Fast approximation algorithms for joint territory design and effort allocation at realistic scale.
relevance: Precedent that the deployment problem needs heuristics at national scale; relevant to the lazy-callback scaling gap.

authors: Andris A. Zoltners; Sally E. Lorimer
title: Sales Territory Alignment: An Overlooked Productivity Tool
venue: Journal of Personal Selling and Sales Management
establishes: Argues misalignment is a large and routinely ignored source of lost sales productivity.
relevance: Motivation and business framing; useful for a non-technical audience.

title: The 2004 ISMS Practice Prize Winner—Sales Territory Design: Thirty Years of Modeling and Implementation
establishes: Thirty-year retrospective on deploying territory-alignment models in industry, including realignment disruption and adoption failure modes.
relevance: The implementation-reality citation. Its cited-by list is the best single entry point to the modern commercial-districting literature.

authors: Murali K. Mantrala; Sönke Albers; Fábio Caldieraro; Ove Jensen; Kissan Joseph; Manfred Krafft; Chakravarthi Narasimhan; Srinath Gopalakrishna; Andris A. Zoltners; Rajiv Lal; Leonard M. Lodish
title: Sales force modeling: State of the field and research agenda
establishes: Survey of the sales-force modelling field with an explicit research agenda.
relevance: Orientation for adjacent work (sizing, compensation, call planning) that the model does not cover.

authors: M. Angélica Salazar–Aguilar; Roger Z. Ríos‐Mercado; Mauricio Cabrera‐Ríos
title: New Models for Commercial Territory Design
establishes: Commercial territory design with multiple balance criteria and dispersion objectives, solved exactly and heuristically.
relevance: Nearest published analogue to the applied setting; useful for defending objective choices.

title: Commercial territory design planning with realignment and disjoint assignment requirements
establishes: Territory design with realignment costs and disjoint-assignment requirements.
relevance: Closest match to a merger realignment: it prices moving units away from an incumbent, which the current model does not.

authors: Hamidreza Validi; Austin Buchanan; Eugene Lykhovyd
title: Imposing Contiguity Constraints in Political Districting Models
establishes: Compares and strengthens contiguity formulations for districting IPs; cut-based and flow-based encodings with computational dominance results.
relevance: Directly supersedes the separator-cut encoding used here. The answer to the national-scale performance gap.

title: The Bargaining Problem
establishes: Axiomatises the two-person bargaining solution: Pareto efficiency, symmetry, scale invariance, IIA select the point maximising the product of gains over the disagreement point.
relevance: The source of the criterion. Note the convexity assumption on the feasible set, which indivisible units violate.

title: Two-Person Cooperative Games
establishes: Extends the bargaining solution to the two-person cooperative game with threats, deriving the disagreement point endogenously.
relevance: Relevant to any argument that the threat point should be modelled rather than assumed. NOTE: OpenAlex records the author as 'John C. Nash'; it is John F. Nash.

title: Other Solutions to Nash's Bargaining Problem
establishes: Replaces IIA with individual monotonicity, selecting the solution that equalises fractions of maximum attainable gain.
relevance: The main alternative criterion. Systematically favours the party with the lower baseline.

title: Proportional Solutions to Bargaining Situations: Interpersonal Utility Comparisons
establishes: Axiomatises proportional/egalitarian solutions, dropping scale invariance in favour of interpersonal utility comparison.
relevance: The reference for any explicit entitlement or seniority weighting, and the natural fallback when the product criterion is undefined.

title: Perfect Equilibrium in a Bargaining Model
establishes: Alternating-offers game with discounting has a unique subgame-perfect equilibrium; its limit supports the Nash solution non-cooperatively.
relevance: Establishes what must be true for a bargaining solution to be descriptive: players must actually make offers. If a committee decides, the criterion is normative instead.

authors: Ken Binmore; Martin J. Osborne; Ariel Rubinstein; Binmore, Ken; Osborne, Martin J.; Rubinstein, Ariel
title: Noncooperative Models of Bargaining
establishes: Survey of non-cooperative bargaining models and the conditions under which they justify cooperative solution concepts.
relevance: Background for the descriptive-versus-normative distinction. Record type is a working paper; the canonical version is the Handbook chapter.

title: Chapter 35 Cooperative models of bargaining
venue: Handbook of game theory and economic applications
establishes: Handbook survey of cooperative bargaining: axioms, solutions, and the relations among them.
relevance: Best single citation for positioning one criterion against the family.

authors: Allan Collard‐Wexler; Gautam Gowrisankaran; Robin S. Lee
title: “Nash-in-Nash” Bargaining: A Microfoundation for Applied Work
establishes: Provides microfoundations for 'Nash-in-Nash' bargaining used in applied IO, clarifying what the bilateral-product assumption requires.
relevance: Template for stating what a bargaining assumption buys and costs in an applied model.

title: Continuum Nash bargaining solutions
venue: Nonlinear Differential Equations and Applications NoDEA
establishes: Characterises the Nash bargaining solution over a continuum of goods; at a zero disagreement point the solution is an optimal-transport map, so the boundary is a Laguerre-cell tessellation.
relevance: Independent corroboration of the d=(0,0) baseline, and the natural route to N>2 wholesalers: semi-discrete transport gives Laguerre cells, contiguous by construction.

title: Nash bargaining theory when the number of alternatives can be finite
establishes: Develops bargaining theory when the alternative set is finite rather than convex.
relevance: The correct citation for a discrete allocation set, where the classical axioms deliver a lottery rather than a point.

title: Alternative characterizations of three bargaining solutions for nonconvex problems
establishes: Characterises Nash, Kalai-Smorodinsky and egalitarian solutions on non-convex problems.
relevance: Companion to Mariotti; needed if a nonzero baseline is retained on a discrete feasible set.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: Consensus of Subjective Probabilities: The Pari-Mutuel Method
establishes: The Eisenberg-Gale convex program, whose optimum is the product-of-utilities allocation.
relevance: Why maximising a product of linear utilities is a well-behaved convex problem; the mathematical ancestor of the log-concavity argument.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: Equity, envy, and efficiency
establishes: Defines envy-freeness and relates equity to efficiency in allocation.
relevance: Origin of the envy criterion that EF1 relaxes.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: Fair Allocation Rules
venue: Handbook of social choice and welfare
establishes: Handbook survey of fair allocation rules and their axiomatic characterisations.
relevance: Reference work for choosing and defending a fairness criterion.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: APX-hardness of maximizing Nash social welfare with indivisible items
establishes: Maximising Nash social welfare with indivisible items is APX-hard.
relevance: Explains why exhaustive validation stops at small n, and why exact solvability here is a property of special structure rather than of the problem.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: Approximating the Nash Social Welfare with Indivisible Items
establishes: First constant-factor approximation for maximising Nash social welfare with indivisible items.
relevance: Establishes the computational standing of the criterion; cite alongside the hardness result.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
authors: Ioannis Caragiannis; David Kurokawa; Hervé Moulin; Ariel D. Procaccia; Nisarg Shah; Junxing Wang
title: The Unreasonable Fairness of Maximum Nash Welfare
venue: ACM Transactions on Economics and Computation
establishes: Maximum Nash welfare (product of utilities, zero baseline) over indivisible goods is Pareto efficient and envy-free up to one good.
relevance: The theorem that licenses an EF1 claim. It requires a ZERO baseline; subtracting a constant from each utility voids the guarantee.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
title: Fair Division in the Internet Age
establishes: Accessible survey of fair division, including maximum Nash welfare and its fairness guarantees.
relevance: The citation to hand a non-specialist or a committee.

section: Fair division and maximum Nash welfare
authors: Georgios Amanatidis; Haris Aziz; Georgios Birmpas; Aris Filos-Ratsikas; Bo Li; Hervé Moulin; Alexandros A. Voudouris; Xiaowei Wu
title: Fair division of indivisible goods: Recent progress and open questions
establishes: Current survey of fair division of indivisible goods: EF1, EFX, MMS, and open problems.
relevance: Fastest route to the state of the art and to what is still unresolved.

authors: Vincent P. Crawford; Hal R. Varian
title: Distortion of preferences and the Nash theory of bargaining
establishes: Agents can gain by misrepresenting preferences to a bargaining solution; the Nash solution is manipulable.
relevance: The reference for reporting incentives. Matters only where inputs are self-reported; cite to establish that the question was considered.

authors: Jan Kronqvist; David E. Bernal; Andreas Lundell; Ignacio E. Grossmann
title: A review and comparison of solvers for convex MINLP
establishes: Benchmarks solvers for convex mixed-integer nonlinear programs, including outer-approximation methods.
relevance: Supports the claim that a concave objective over a MILP-representable set is the tractable class, and guides solver choice.

title: Mixed-integer nonlinear programming 2018
establishes: Survey of mixed-integer nonlinear programming: formulations, algorithms, software.
relevance: General MINLP citation for methods sections.
